title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: John xvii. 6, 15, 24 and Matt. xiii. 11 — order: persons given to Christ first; then Spirit opens hearts to faith; then he sustains them; God does not elect from foresight of free-will faith
pass_a_gloss: The same is plain Joann. xvii. 6. Where Christ says that he has manifested the name of his Father unto the men whom he gave him from the world. And vers. 15. He asks specially for these, that they be kept from that evil one, and unto everlasting glory be led vers. 24. Unto this also those words of Matth. xiii. 11. avail. Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, unto them it is not given. In which places the order itself is diligently to be observed. First, certain persons are given unto Christ to be quickened and saved from the special good pleasure of God the Father. Then Christ by a special operation of his Spirit opens these ones' hearts, that they may conceive saving knowledge of God and faith. At length he so governs and sustains the illuminated and converted that by no temptations of the devil they be seduced unto destruction. God therefore does not look to see who by their free choice excited by grace will believe and persevere, and from this foresight elect them, others being passed over, but he elects certain ones from his mere good pleasure, and gives them unto Christ, unto whom Christ inspires faith that they may approach unto God, and implants perseverance that they may not withdraw from him.
pass_b_english: The same is plain in John xvii. 6, where Christ says he has manifested his Father's name to the men the Father gave him from the world. And verse 15: he asks specially for these, that they be kept from that evil one, and led to everlasting glory (verse 24). Matthew xiii. 11 serves the same point: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; to them it is not given. In these places the order itself must be carefully watched. First, certain persons are given to Christ to be quickened and saved from God the Father's special good pleasure. Then Christ, by a special operation of his Spirit, opens their hearts so they conceive saving knowledge of God and faith. At last he so governs and sustains the illuminated and converted that no devil's temptations seduce them to ruin. God does not look to see who by free choice excited by grace will believe and persevere, and from that foresight elect them while passing others over. He elects some from his mere good pleasure, and gives them to Christ; Christ inspires faith in them that they may come to God, and implants perseverance that they may not withdraw from him.
source_text: Idem patet Joann. xvii. 6. Ubi Christus dicit se manifestasse nomen Patris sui hominibus, quos dedit illi de mundo. Et vers. 15. Rogat specialim pro hisce, ut serventur a malo illo, et ad gloriam aeternam perducantur vers. 24. Huc etiam faciunt illa verba Matth. xiii. 11. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum, illis non est datum. In quibus locis ipse ordo est diligenter observandus. Primo, certae quaedam personae dantur Christo vivificandae et salvandae ex speciali beneplacito Dei Patris. Tum Christus speciali operatione Spiritus sui aperit horum corda, ut salutiferam Dei cognitionem ac fidem concipiant. Tandem illuminatos et conversos ita gubernat et sustentat, ut nullis diaboli tentationibus ad interitum seducantur. Non ergo speculatur Deus quinam sunt libero suo arbitrio per gratiam excitato credituri et perseveraturi, et ex hac praevisione aliis praeteritis eos eligit, sed eligit quosdam ex mero suo beneplacito, donatque Christo, quibus Christus inspirat fidem ut accedant ad Deum, et indit perseverantiam ne recedant ab eo.
